paper_metadata.title: A 57.9-to-68.3GHz 24.6mW Frequency Synthesizer with In-Phase Injection-Coupled QVCO in 65nm CMOS Xiang Yi, Chirn Chye Boon, Hang Liu, Jia Fu Lin, Jian Cheng Ong, Wei Meng Lim

figures.label: Fig. 20
figures.caption: Figure 20.5.1: The frequency synthesizer and QVCO.

references.sentence: The block diagram of the frequency synthesizer is shown in Fig. 20.5.1.
The schematic of the QVCO is also depicted in Fig. 20.5.1.
The operation of the diode-connected transistor MC2 in the coupling network in Fig. 20.5.1 will be analyzed first in order to understand the in-phase coupling in this QVCO.
When the QVCO is operating, the phase of drain and source voltages of MC2 are 0 and -π/2 respectively, as shown in Fig. 20.5.2(a).

The current Iinj, injected into the node I+ from the coupling network, is equal to IC1 - IC2, Therefore, the injection current Iinj is in-phase with the tank current Itank, as shown in Fig. 20.5.2(b).
Figure 20.5.3 shows the schematics of the DCML and ILFD dividers.
The programmable self-correcting low spur CP, shown in Fig. 20.5.4, is modified from [3].
Secondly, V1 can be regarded as V2 after a unity-gain amplifier, as shown in the simplified equivalent schematic in Fig. 20.5.4.
Figure 20.5.4 depicts the simulated waveforms of Vctrl when it is connected to V1 and V2 respectively.
Figure 20.5.7 shows the die micrograph of the standalone QVCO and the complete PLL, which occupy 0.26×0.15mm2 and 0.32×0.60mm2, respectively.
As depicted in Fig. 20.5.5(a), the measured QVCO phase noises for a 62.66GHz carrier are -94.2 and -115.0dBc/Hz at 1 and 10MHz offset, respectively.
The phase noise of the PLL, shown in Fig. 20.5.5(b), is -91.0dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset when carrier frequency is 62.64GHz.
The measured QVCO and PLL performance are summarized and compared with state-of-the-art works in Fig. 20.5.6.
